chapter: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
title: Music Town's location and moving his present house
summary: Music Town stood at Jefferson and Normandie; in 1952 he bought and moved a large house and describes its size.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So that was very close to the place where you later had Music Town then, right?
Music Town was at Jefferson and Normandie.
No, about two blocks. I walked right around there, back and forth. Yeah.
You were living there when you had Music Town?
Yeah, I didn't move over here...I bought this building in '52.

Yes, it is a nice big place. But I bought this place on...Witmer and...Wilshire. See, they wanted to put a parking lot there, and I was in Music Town, and I went...I was looking for a duplex over here 'cause I wanted my sister downstairs, and I was going to live upstairs, and I lookin' around for a duplex, and I saw this in the paper, and I went over there, and I bought it and moved it over here. Yeah, it cost me $6,500 to move it, and I had to pay about five thousand dollars for moving the telephone poles. It was so big, you know, and the telephone wires,they had to cut 'em and let the house by, and put 'em back together and everything. Then I bought the lot, and it cost me a lot to put it back together--I mean to put it right back together like it was.
But it's such a lovely, spacious place, though. The rooms are so big.
Oh, it's a big place--two thousand square feet I got in here.
And that's just one-fourth because there's four units here.
That's just one... Yeah. Well, I got a little bigger room than the rest of them 'cause I got that music room over there, sticks out over the driveway. All the rest of it's the same, though.
It's really wonderful, though. It has the feeling of a very spacious house, and...
It's bigger than a house. I know a lot of people that claim they got a big house. I got two thousand feet, and the average big home is about sixteen hundred, you know.
Yes, it's eighty-one feet from here to... I walk it ten or twelve times a day .....[almost] half a mile. (Chuckles)
